title: Waves and Sound
intro: A wave transfers energy without transferring the medium as a whole. Transverse: displacement ⊥ travel (string, EM). Longitudinal: // travel (sound in air — compressions and rarefactions).

cards.title: 3.1 Waves
body: Anything that moves up and down or back and forth in a rhythmic way is vibrating.
Vibrations are involved in sound, heat, electricity, and light.

cards.title: Waves: fuller notes
body: A **wave** carries energy from place to place without carrying matter. **Transverse** waves vibrate at right angles to the direction of travel (light, water ripples); **longitudinal** waves vibrate along it, as compressions and rarefactions (sound).
**Amplitude** = maximum displacement; **wavelength λ** = distance between two neighbouring crests; **frequency f** = waves per second (Hz); **period** T = 1/f. **Wave equation:** v = fλ.

cards.title: Worked example: the wave equation
cards.problem: A sound of frequency 170 Hz travels in air at 340 m/s. Find its wavelength and period.

cards.title: Waves & sound
body: v=fλ. Transverse vs longitudinal. Sound needs a medium; louder ↔ larger amplitude.
Pitch ↔ frequency. Reflection = echo; higher T → slightly faster sound in air.

cards.title: Interference & beats intro
body: Two close frequencies → beats; beat frequency |f₁−f₂|.

cards.title: 3.2 Sound
body: Music from a kirar, a guitar and a drum are produced by the parts of these instruments that vibrate.
Second, the energy is transferred from the source in the form of longitudinal sound waves.

cards.title: Sound
body: Sound is a longitudinal wave made by vibrating objects. It needs a **medium** (solid, liquid or gas) and cannot travel in a vacuum. It travels fastest in solids and slowest in gases; in air about 340 m/s.

cards.title: Common mix-ups in Waves and Sound
body: Write one idea students often confuse with this topic, then the correct distinction.
Example pattern: “Looks like X, but actually Y because …”
Teaching the difference is better than re-reading the page.

cards.title: 3.3 Behaviour of Sound Waves
body: A ticking stopwatch, cardboard tubes, a wooden board, and a piece of cardboard.
Reverberation is repeated echoes of sound.

cards.title: Worked example: echo
cards.problem: A student claps in front of a cliff and hears the echo 0.50 s later. Speed of sound 340 m/s. How far away is the cliff?

steps.text: The sound travels to the cliff and back: total distance = v × t = 340 × 0.50 = 170 m.

why: Textbook p.147: The medium can be a material medium such as a solid, a liquid, a gas or it can be a vacuum.

questions.q: What happens to sound in a vacuum?
why: Answer D: It cannot travel (no medium)
Textbook p.226: A sound wave transports its energy through a vacuum.
